slides.title: A Large Language Model-Driven Agent-Based Modeling Framework with Multi-Round Communication for Simulating Vaccine Opinion Dynamics
slides.tldr: LLM-DRIVEN AGENT-BASED MODELING FOR OPINION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research introduces an LLM-integrated agent-based modeling framework to simulate how cognitive modules influence macro-level opinion dynamics, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: An LLM-driven agent-based framework simulates how cognitive modules influence vaccine opinion dynamics and social polarization.
card.key_idea: Integrates Qwen3-8B into ABM using multi-round dialogues, reflection, and memory modules to model non-linear social influence and opinion shifts among heterogeneous agents.
card.evaluation: Simulated 95 agents across four scenarios (baseline, memory, diversity, combined) using synthetic population data; analyzed vaccination rates and opinion polarization.
card.limitation: Small simulation size (95 agents) due to high LLM computational costs and absence of opinion leaders.

slides.title: AgoraSim: A Hybrid Agent-Based Modeling Framework
slides.highlight: AgoraSim provides a framework for social reaction analysis by mixing LLM agents with classical agents, supporting the meso- and societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: AgoraSim is a hybrid agent-based modeling framework for analyzing social reactions to natural-language scenarios.
card.key_idea: It mixes LLM, VLM, and classical rule-based agents in ratio-controlled populations, mapping open-ended language behaviors into a shared structured action space for comparison against reference dynamics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a congestion-pricing scenario walkthrough; focuses on exploratory trajectory comparison and auditability rather than predictive accuracy or benchmarked datasets.
card.limitation: Outputs are synthetic and may reflect model biases or stereotypes; lacks external validity and requires empirical validation for real-world claims.

slides.title: China unveils ultra-realistic humanoid robots for companionship
slides.highlight: The development of ultra-realistic humanoid robots for companionship is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Realbotix Partners with Bloom to Launch UK Pilot Using Humanoid Robots to Combat Elderly Social Isolation
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOTS TO COMBAT ELDERLY SOCIAL ISOLATION
slides.highlight: This pilot uses humanoid robots to address social isolation among the elderly, providing a relevant case study for RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Multimodal Voice Activity Projection for Turn-Taking in Social Robots with Voice-Activity-Related Pretrained Encoders
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Multimodal Voice Activity Projection framework using audio-visual inputs and inter-speaker attention to project future voice activity, supporting HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: A multimodal framework for social robots to predict turn-taking by projecting future voice activity.
card.key_idea: MM-VAP uses LoRA-adapted, speech-activity pretrained audio-visual encoders (TalkNet/WhisperFlamingo) with inter-speaker attention and a semantic consistency loss to project joint voice activity states.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NoXi, NoXi+J, and Haru EDR corpora using Accuracy and F1-score; outperformed baselines in several turn-taking events.
card.limitation: The approach was only validated offline and not under real-time conditions due to high computational resource requirements.

slides.title: Responsible Personalisation: The Double-Edged Sword of Personalisation in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a lifecycle-based framework to analyze ethical risks in personalized human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for analyzing ethical risks in personalized HRI, emphasizing how robot embodiment amplifies these risks.
card.key_idea: A lifecycle-based, context-sensitive framework combining six development phases with interaction characteristics (duration and domain) to systematically map and mitigate ethical risks in personalized robotics.
card.evaluation: Developed through interdisciplinary expert workshops and a review of current state-of-the-art HRI and HCI literature.
card.limitation: The work provides a conceptual and analytical framework rather than empirical testing of the proposed design recommendations.

slides.title: LLM-powered reasoning in agent-based modeling
slides.highlight: The HALE framework integrates LLMs into agent-based modeling to better predict human decision-making, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: HALE integrates LLM reasoning into agent-based modeling to dynamically predict human mobility changes during epidemics.
card.key_idea: A hybrid framework where LLMs act as a feedback loop, adjusting activity-based temporal network links for demographic subpopulations based on perceived disease threat levels.
card.evaluation: Simulated COVID-19 in Salt Lake County (Sept 2021–Feb 2022) using Llama 3.1; HALE better captured epidemic peak and size than ABM-only baselines.
card.limitation: LLM inference is sensitive to prompts and temperature; it may lack sufficient information for very small municipalities.

slides.title: Validating Virtual Reality for Studying Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction in Socially Aware Robot Navigation
slides.tldr: VR VALIDATED FOR SOCIAL HRI STUDY
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that VR can reliably capture multimodal interaction dynamics and perceived social awareness in robot navigation, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: VR is validated as a reliable platform for studying multimodal human-robot co-navigation and social awareness.
card.key_idea: A VR prototype replicating a real-world arena was used to compare human locomotion trajectories and head-orientation cues during orthogonal crossing and pass-by interactions with a PR2 robot.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects study (N=21) comparing VR and real-world settings via Likert scales, trajectory analysis, and head-pose data. Results show consistent behavioral patterns across environments.
card.limitation: Lack of auditory cues, restricted peripheral field of view, and reduced naturalness of movement compared to real-world walking.

slides.title: HumAIN: Human-Aware Implicit Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: The HumAIN framework uses knowledge distillation to integrate implicit social cues like gait and orientation into robot planning, supporting socially compliant navigation. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: HumAIN enables socially compliant robot navigation by distilling privileged human skeletal cues into a lightweight vision-only model.
card.key_idea: A transformer-based teacher model learns social representations from multi-modal data (RGB, skeletal keypoints, robot state), which are then distilled into a student model using only RGB images.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on SCAND and OOD datasets against ViNT, NoMaD, GNM, and HST+MPC; improved trajectory prediction metrics by an average of 29.8%.
card.limitation: Not yet robust for unconstrained real-world environments, specifically crowded scenes, occlusions, and datasets biased by teleoperator preferences.
